plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to zero.
Reduce broad index (SPY) to 20% to lower concentration.
Increase income ETF (QQQI) to 15% for stability.
Hold remaining cash buffer for safety.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation with low drawdown.
conservative.read: This plan aims for a low ~1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leverage and focusing on stable assets, leading to lower potential drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to low single digits.
Reduce broad index (SPY) to 25% to address concentration.
Add income ETF (QQQI) to 10% for diversification.
Initiate a new position in AAPL (4%) as a quality tech addition.
This plan balances growth with risk reduction, aiming for steady gains.
balanced.read: This plan targets a ~2.5% monthly return. It seeks growth by maintaining some tech exposure while reducing leverage and concentration, aiming for a risk-first approach.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to capture upside.
Trim broad index (SPY) to 25% and income (QQQI) to 5% to concentrate capital.
Initiate a new position in AAPL (6%) as a high-conviction tech play.
This plan aggressively leans into leverage and concentration for maximum growth potential.
Expect higher volatility and potential for larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This plan targets a ~4% monthly return, accepting significantly higher risk. It maximizes leverage and concentration in high-conviction names, including leveraged ETFs, which amplifies both gains and losses. Daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs can lead to decay.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) and high-beta tech (CRWD, SNOW, SMH).
Reduce broad index (SPY) to 20% to minimize volatility.
Increase income ETF (QQQI) to 40% for maximum monthly distributions.
This plan prioritizes steady income generation and capital preservation.
Focus is on reliable cash flow over aggressive growth.
income.read: This plan targets a low ~1% monthly return, focusing on stable income. It minimizes risk by eliminating leverage and volatile single stocks, prioritizing consistent distributions from income-focused ETFs. NAV can still decline in market downturns.
